Panel sheet — loop

Built · 96.3s E001 Structural ending

This is the built episode, not a proposal. All 24 panels are the frames from Figma, cut to the recorded VO and rendered to 96.3 seconds. Scene 23 reuses scene 5's audio. Screen times below are the actual timings from the render, so a long number means that panel genuinely sits there.

Episode ID
E001-loop
Term
loop
Cast
Dev 1 (asks) · Dev 2 (says it first) · Dev 3 (closes the loop)
Ending engine
Structural — the loop restarts. Not reusable elsewhere; it works because the term is loop.
The want
He wants to not look stupid.
Teach
A loop is stepwise, self-checked work with nobody in the middle; the finish line is the thing you write; a step cap and a budget exist and he set neither. Stated at 7, shown at 8, applied at 11, named at 17.
Explanation
Three rungs of the same term, hard to easy — dense (5) → plain (7) → shown (8). The downshift is triggered by him, not volunteered by the machine. The visual stays simple at every rung: pompous words over a dumb clear picture is where the comedy lives.
Animated
Not yet. Every panel here is a still. The seven screen panels are where the simple explanation visual goes — 5 and 8 are the two longest holds in the episode, which is exactly where a static frame is felt.
Build
Figma frames exported as SVG, animated in Remotion. The visuals aren’t designed yet — that happens once the panel frames exist. Reuse the spring config and useCount odometer from tetriz-launch-video-v4.2, but not its LoopsSequence visuals, which are the product dashboard.
Runtime
96.3s. Cut from Whisper word-level timestamps: each panel starts on its first spoken word and holds until the next line begins, which gives every panel its tail for free.

How to review this

Select the panel row and comment on it. Four things are worth your comment — everything else can wait for a later pass.

  1. 01Does the term actually land? If you didn't know it before, do you now — and from which panel?
  2. 02Is the information flow broken anywhere? The usual failure is a character not understanding something plainer than what they themselves just said. For each panel, check that person has a stated reason to know or not know.
  3. 03Does the ending turn? Setup plus violation. An observation is not a gag, however true.
  4. 04Is any number ambiguous about which way the joke runs?

Don't polish prose yet — beats and information flow first; wording is cheap to fix once the structure is agreed. And if you want Claude to act on a thread rather than just Sejal, mention @claude in it — otherwise it can read the comment but not reply.

Author checks

Cleared before this went up for review.

  • ✓The want is named, and the ending is a consequence of it.
  • ✓The signature fires once, at the top — except here, where its repetition is the punchline.
  • ✓Every AI speaks in its fixed register. The burnt-out one is shortest.
  • ✓Nothing requires a previous episode to make sense.
  • ✓No explanation is attached to the script.
  • ✓Reused framings are marked, which is what keeps art cost down.
Panel image slots stay empty until the art gate. Once panels exist they drop into the same rows, and this page becomes the second review surface too — one artifact, one set of comment threads, two gates.
